summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Neoplastic transformation results from loss of contact inhibition and dysregulation of cellular proto-oncogenes or tumor suppressors. Malignant tumors exhibit Metastasis—spreading to distant organs via bloodstream/lymph. Diagnostic modalities include biopsy, CT, MRI, and monoclonal antibodies. Therapies encompass surgery, radiotherapy, spindle-inhibiting chemotherapy, and alpha-interferon immunotherapy.

conceptBreakdown.content:
### 7.1 Hallmarks of Neoplasia
- **Loss of Contact Inhibition**: Normal eukaryotic cells arrest proliferation when contacting neighboring cells. Cancer cells lose contact inhibition, continuing uncontrolled mitosis to form unorganized cell masses (**Tumors**).
- **Benign vs. Malignant Tumors**:
  - *Benign Tumors*: Remain confined to original anatomical site enclosed in a fibrous capsule; do not invade surrounding tissues or spread to distant sites; cause minimal damage.
  - *Malignant Tumors (Neoplasms)*: Proliferate aggressively, invade local tissues, starve normal cells by competing for nutrients, and display **Metastasis** (shed cells enter bloodstream/lymph to seed secondary tumors in distant organs).

### 7.2 Carcinogens & Oncogenesis
1. **Physical Carcinogens**: Ionizing radiation (X-rays, $\gamma$-rays) induce double-strand DNA breaks; non-ionizing UV radiation causes thymine dimer formation.
2. **Chemical Carcinogens**: **Tobacco smoke** chemicals (**3,4-Benzopyrene**, $N$-nitrosamines) cause lung, throat, and bladder cancers; asbestos and coal tar.
3. **Biological Carcinogens**: Oncogenic viruses carrying viral oncogenes (*v-onc*); mutation or amplification of cellular **Proto-Oncogenes (*c-onc*)** or inactivation of **Tumor Suppressor Genes (*p53*, *Rb*)** transforms normal cells into cancer.

### 7.3 Diagnostic & Therapeutic Modalities
- **Diagnostics**: Biopsy and histopathological examination; blood and bone marrow smears for elevated leukemic blast cells; **Computed Tomography (CT)** (3D X-ray reconstruction); **Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI)** (uses non-ionizing magnetic fields); Monoclonal antibodies.
- **Therapeutics**:
  - *Surgery*: En bloc surgical resection of localized primary tumor masses.
  - *Radiotherapy*: Targeted lethal ionizing radiation destroying tumor cells.
  - *Chemotherapy*: Cytotoxic antineoplastic drugs, including plant vinca alkaloids (**Vinblastine** and **Vincristine** from *Catharanthus roseus* / Madagascar periwinkle) that arrest mitotic spindle assembly.
  - *Immunotherapy*: Administration of **$\alpha$-Interferon** (a biological response modifier) to activate the patient's own NK cells and cytotoxic T-cells to destroy malignant cells.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Angiogenesis and VEGF
conceptBreakdown.title: Angiogenesis and VEGF
conceptBreakdown.content: Growing tumors secrete Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor (VEGF) to stimulate tumor angiogenesis (new capillary network sprouting) to supply oxygen and nutrients, targeted clinically by anti-angiogenic monoclonal antibodies (e.g., Bevacizumab).

conceptBreakdown.heading: p53: Guardian of the Genome
conceptBreakdown.title: p53: Guardian of the Genome
conceptBreakdown.content: The p53 tumor suppressor protein halts the cell cycle at G1/S upon sensing DNA damage, activating DNA repair pathways or triggering apoptosis; mutated in over 50% of human cancers.
